name: skye-open-source-spectacle-recipes
purpose: Concrete open-source frontend recipes agents must pull when the user asks for advanced effects. These recipes are not SkyeSol styling; they are implementation primitives.
rule: Pick recipes by behavior first, then apply brand taste. Do not make everything look like SkyeSol.

imports: import { motion, useMotionValue, useSpring, useScroll, useTransform } from 'framer-motion';
recipes.useWhen: The page needs premium UI interaction, cursor-responsive layers, spring movement, layout transitions, or scroll-bound transforms.
avoid: static CSS pretending to be Framer Motion
recipes.starter: Use motion components for CTA/surface panels; use useMotionValue/useSpring for cursor glow; use useScroll/useTransform for scroll-bound depth.

recipes.useWhen: The first viewport needs a living object, shader field, spatial product symbol, particle system, or interactive canvas.
avoid: flat CSS glow sold as Three.js
recipes.starter: Build one dominant product object or shader field; bind camera/object motion to pointer and time.

recipes.useWhen: A Three/R3F scene needs cinematic lighting, depth, bloom, floating objects, stars, camera helpers, or visual finish.
recipes.starter: Wrap the scene with EffectComposer, add Bloom/Vignette, use Float/Stars/PerspectiveCamera to make the visual feel staged.

recipes.useWhen: The page needs a scroll-led story, sticky/pinned sections, scrubbed transitions, rails, staged proof, or cinematic funnel.
avoid: basic anchor scroll presented as GSAP
recipes.starter: Create Lenis raf loop, bind ScrollTrigger.update, and stage sections with scrubbed opacity/position/progress rails.

recipes.useWhen: A 3D scene or hero needs director-like keyframed parameters, camera beats, or reusable art-directed states.
mustShow: Theatre project/sheet or documented reason not to load studio in production
avoid: shipping studio UI to buyers by accident
recipes.starter: Use getProject for scene state; wire sheet values to camera, light, object rotation, or section beats.

imports: Use generated screenshot assets from browser QA; render them as first-class product media.
recipes.useWhen: The user has an app, dashboard, website, game, or tool where the real surface matters.
mustShow: caption proving what surface is shown
avoid: fake UI if real UI exists
recipes.starter: Capture real surfaces with Playwright, place them in an angled/staged gallery or first viewport subject.

imports: Use Playwright recordVideo or dense browser-action frames, encode with ffmpeg, render with <video autoplay muted loop playsinline>.
recipes.useWhen: The user asks for actual screenshots to become animated proof, or the page claims the app performs a workflow.
mustShow: video first in the proof stage
browser check that video is visible and playing
avoid: static landing screenshots called workflow proof
headline-first hero when actual surface proof was requested
recipes.starter: Use Playwright to goto/click/fill/scroll/submit through the claimed flow, record video or dense frames, encode H.264 with -movflags +faststart, render MP4/WebM, then verify readyState/currentTime/paused/visible in browser E2E.

imports: Call design_logo_manifest before drawing or generating any mark.
recipes.useWhen: Any page has a logo, brand mark, wordmark, favicon, nav identity, or product mark.
mustShow: transparent/floating placement when the asset supports it
clean wordmark fallback when no asset exists
avoid: replacing finished logos with generic initials
recipes.starter: Use the approved logo asset path from design_logo_manifest. If there is no exact asset, use typography-only wordmark plus parent brand endorsement rather than inventing a permanent emblem.

recipes.useWhen: The user asks for visible scrollbar, neon UI chrome, cursor trail, or tactile premium interaction.
avoid: thin invisible scrollbar on scroll-led pages
recipes.starter: Use CSS scrollbar thumb/track styling with a visible rgba track, neon gradient thumb, glow box-shadow, and a fixed pointer-events-none Framer Motion glow following pointer spring values.

recipes.useWhen: The user asks for glowing text, neon text, text effects, split reveals, or high-impact display type.
recipes.starter: Use one hero-scale glow/shimmer effect; animate reveal with Framer Motion or GSAP split-line timing.
